name: Economic Order Quantity (EOQ)
description: Computes the economic order quantity as the square root of two times annual demand times order cost, divided by holding cost per unit. It gives the order size that minimizes total annual ordering plus holding costs.
notes: Assumes steady demand, constant costs, and no shortages; order cost is per order and holding cost is per unit per year. Real order sizes may be rounded to practical batch quantities.

name: EOQ Minimum Total Cost
description: Computes the minimum total annual inventory cost at the economic order quantity as the square root of two times annual demand times order cost times holding cost per unit. At the optimal order size, annual ordering and holding costs are equal and their sum is minimized.
notes: This gives the combined ordering plus holding cost, excluding purchase price of the goods; it uses the same assumptions as the EOQ model. Order cost is per order and holding cost is per unit per year.

name: Reorder Point (with Safety Stock)
description: Computes the reorder point as daily demand times lead time in days, plus safety stock. It is the inventory level at which a new order should be placed so that stock lasts through the replenishment lead time, with a buffer for variability.
notes: Daily demand and lead time must use the same time unit (days); safety stock is added to protect against demand or lead-time variation. The result is in inventory units.

name: Labor Productivity
description: Computes labor productivity as value added divided by the number of employees, indicating the average economic output generated per worker.
notes: Value added and headcount (or average headcount) should be measured over the same period. Higher labor productivity generally reflects greater capital investment, skill, or process efficiency per worker.

name: Process Capability Index Cp
description: Gives how many times the process spread fits inside the tolerance, ignoring centring; 1.33 is a common minimum.
notes: Cpk also penalises an off-centre process.

name: Rolled Throughput Yield
description: Gives the chance a unit passes every process step right the first time.
notes: Hidden rework makes RTY much lower than final yield.

name: Acceptance Sampling: Probability of Acceptance
description: Gives the chance a lot is accepted when n items are inspected and at most c defectives are allowed — one point of the operating characteristic curve.
notes: Plot it against p to see how well the plan separates good and bad lots.

name: X-bar Chart Upper Control Limit
description: Gives the upper control limit for subgroup means on a Shewhart X-bar chart; the lower limit subtracts the same amount.
notes: A₂ depends on subgroup size: 1.880 for n = 2, 0.577 for n = 5.

name: Taguchi Quality Loss
description: Gives the economic loss of a part that deviates from target, growing with the square of the deviation (Taguchi).
notes: Even in-tolerance parts cost something if off target.

name: Safety Stock (Demand Variability)
description: Gives the extra stock that covers demand swings during the replenishment lead time at the service level set by z.
notes: z = 1.645 gives a 95 % cycle service level.

name: Safety Stock (Demand and Lead-Time Variability)
description: Gives safety stock when both daily demand and the lead time vary.
notes: Unreliable suppliers (large lead-time spread) often matter more than demand swings.

name: Newsvendor Critical Ratio
description: Gives the optimal probability of not running out for a one-time order: underage cost / (underage + overage cost).
notes: Stock up to the demand quantile equal to this ratio.

name: Newsvendor Optimal Order (Normal Demand)
description: Gives the order quantity that maximises expected profit when demand is normally distributed.
notes: Here about 543 units, above mean demand because running out costs more than leftovers.

name: EOQ with Planned Backorders
expression: sqrt(2 * d * s / h) * sqrt((h + b) / b)
description: Extends the economic order quantity to the case where shortages are allowed and filled later.
notes: Cheaper backorders allow larger orders.

name: Economic Production Quantity
description: Gives the best batch size when items are produced gradually rather than delivered at once.
notes: Reduces to the EOQ as the production rate becomes very large.

name: Little's Law
description: Gives the average number of items in a stable system: L = λW (Little 1961).
notes: Holds for any queue, warehouse or production line in steady state, whatever the distributions.

name: Learning Curve Unit Time (Wright)
description: Gives the time for unit n when each doubling of output cuts unit time to a fixed percentage (Wright 1936, aircraft production).
notes: With an 80 % curve the 8th unit takes 51.2 hours.

name: Cumulative Time for n Units (Learning Curve)
description: Adds the unit times of the first n units on a Wright learning curve.
notes: Used to quote fixed-price contracts for series production.

name: Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)
description: Multiplies availability, performance and quality to rate how productively equipment is used.
notes: 85 % is often cited as world class.

name: Takt Time
description: Gives the pace at which one unit must be finished to meet demand.
notes: Here 1.5 minutes per unit; lines are balanced so no station exceeds takt.

name: Process Capability Index Cpk
description: Measures how well a centred-or-not process fits within its specification limits.
notes: Cpk ≥ 1.33 is a common requirement; Six Sigma corresponds to Cpk = 2 (1.5 with the conventional shift).

name: Defects per Million Opportunities (DPMO)
description: Normalises defect counts to one million opportunities, the Six Sigma quality scale.
notes: 3.4 DPMO is the Six Sigma target.

name: Sigma Level from DPMO
description: Converts DPMO to a process sigma level including the conventional 1.5-sigma long-term shift.
notes: 3.4 DPMO is 6 sigma; 3000 DPMO is about 4.25 sigma.

name: Gross Margin Return on Inventory (GMROI)
description: Gives the gross margin earned per unit of money invested in inventory.
notes: Retailers look for values above about 3.

name: Inventory Shrinkage Rate
description: Gives inventory lost to theft, damage or errors as a share of sales.
notes: Retail averages are around 1.5 %.

name: Revenue per Available Room (RevPAR)
description: Multiplies the average room rate by occupancy, the hotel industry's headline performance measure.
notes: Equals room revenue divided by all rooms available.

name: Airline Load Factor
description: Gives the share of seat capacity filled by paying passengers.
notes: Airlines typically need 70–80 % to break even.

name: Food Cost Percentage
description: Gives the cost of food used as a share of food sales.
notes: Restaurants commonly aim for 28–35 %.

name: Prime Cost Percentage
description: Adds food, beverage and labour costs and compares them with sales.
notes: Keeping prime cost below about 60–65 % is a common restaurant rule.

name: Employee Turnover Rate
description: Divides the number of leavers by the average headcount.
notes: Replacing an employee commonly costs a sizeable fraction of a year's salary.

name: Absenteeism Rate
description: Gives the share of scheduled working time lost to unplanned absence.
notes: Rates of 1.5–3 % are typical in many countries.

name: Click-Through Rate (CTR)
description: Divides clicks by impressions for an ad or search result.
notes: Search ads average a few percent; display ads well under 1 %.

name: Cost per Acquisition (CPA)
description: Divides advertising spend by the number of conversions (sales, sign-ups).
notes: Compare with customer lifetime value to judge a campaign.

name: Net Promoter Score
description: Subtracts the percentage of detractors from the percentage of promoters (Reichheld 2003).
notes: Ranges from −100 to +100; here 34.

name: Total Addressable Market (Bottom-Up)
description: Estimates a total addressable market from the bottom up: customers × purchases per customer × price.
notes: Narrow it to the serviceable and obtainable market with realistic shares.

name: Project Loan Life Coverage Ratio
expression: sum(k, 1, len(cf), at(cf, k) / (1 + r)^k) / debt

variables.label: Cash flow available for debt service each year

description: Divides the present value of cash flow available for debt service over the loan life by the debt outstanding (project finance).
notes: Lenders typically require at least 1.2–1.4.

name: Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC)
description: Divides risk-adjusted earnings (after expected loss) by the economic capital the activity consumes.
notes: A loan adds value if RAROC exceeds the bank's hurdle rate.

name: Merton Model Distance to Default
description: Gives the number of standard deviations the firm's assets are above the default point in Merton's structural model (the basis of Moody's KMV).
notes: The default probability is N(−DD).

name: Merton Model Default Probability
description: Gives the probability that assets fall below the debt at the horizon in Merton's model.
notes: About 4.6 % here. Equity is a call option on the firm's assets with the debt as strike.

name: Cost-Plus Sale Price (Murabaha)
description: Gives the sale price in a cost-plus sale in which the seller discloses cost and mark-up, the basis of murabaha financing in Islamic finance.
notes: Usually paid in instalments; the mark-up is fixed at the outset.

name: Invoice Factoring Advance and Fee
description: Gives the cash received up front when selling an invoice to a factor, less the time-based fee.
notes: The reserve (15 % here) is returned when the customer pays.

name: Early Payment Discount Annual Cost (2/10 net 30)
description: Gives the annualised cost of not taking a trade discount such as "2/10 net 30".
notes: Skipping a 2/10 net 30 discount costs about 37 % a year, so borrowing to pay early usually pays.

name: Contribution per Constrained Resource
description: Ranks products when one resource is scarce: contribution margin per unit of the bottleneck (theory of constraints).
notes: Produce the products with the highest value first.
